materials.analysis: Design a 3-year Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) ladder with staggered maturities, allocating 5% of the portfolio to Gold in the 3rd year for inflation hedging. Specifically, allocate 7% to the 1st-year TIPS, 10% to the 2nd-year TIPS, and 3% to the 3rd-year TIPS. The allocation to Gold in the 3rd year, 5%, does not exceed the 15% raw materials limit, but it is important to note that this inflation hedge is not expected to provide the same return as the TIPS. The inflation correlation rationale for using Gold is that it tends to perform well during periods of high inflation as a safe-haven asset, and its price is less correlated with traditional stock and bond markets, serving as a distinct diversification tool. The TIPS ladder provides a relatively stable and predictable income stream, with maturities staggered to align with the expected return cycles.

The reason for this allocation is that Gold and Silver have historically seen returns positively correlated with inflation, serving as a hedge against inflationary pressures.
